terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js starts your API on a free port, tries a few sign-ins and prints what came back, with your log lines among them.

tasks.title: Check a sign-in the same way every time
tasks.description:
Implement `checkSignIn(staff, email, password)` in `src/signIn.js`. `staff` is a staff store.

- find the member with the store's `findByEmail()`, which ignores case
- when the password is theirs, return them as `{ id, name, email, role }`, without the hash
- otherwise return `null`: a wrong password and an email nobody has give the same answer
- both of those take as long: an unknown email still checks the password against a hash

The check signs in against staff of its own, with right and wrong passwords and an unknown email, and counts how much hashing each attempt does.
nextSteps: Check the password against their hash with `verifyPassword`.
Make an unknown email check a password too.
Return the member without the hash, or `null`.
hints: Two answers must be the same: what comes back, and how long it takes. The lesson part on the same amount of work says why.
When nobody has the email, there is no hash to check against. Make one stand-in hash once, when the module loads, and check the typed password against that instead.

`const STAND_IN = hashPassword('...')` at the top, then `verifyPassword(password, member ? member.passwordHash : STAND_IN)`. Return `publicStaff(member)` only when there is a member and the check passed.

tasks.title: Add the sign-in route
tasks.description:
Implement `signInRouter(staff)` in `src/routes/signIn.js`. It returns a router with `POST /sign-in`, whose body is `{ email, password }`:

- when either is missing, not text, or empty, answer `400` with `{ "error": { "code": "bad_sign_in", "message": "..." } }`
- when `checkSignIn` finds the member, answer `200` with `{ "staff": { id, name, email, role } }`
- otherwise answer `401` with `{ "error": { "code": "wrong_sign_in", "message": "..." } }`, exactly the same answer for a wrong password and for an email nobody has

Then mount it in `createApp` with `app.use(signInRouter(staff))`, before the 404 catch-all. The check sends sign-ins of every kind to an app with staff of its own.
nextSteps: Make a router with a `POST /sign-in` route and return it.
Refuse a body without an email and a password.
Mount the router in `createApp`, then run `node try.js`.
hints: The route has three ways out: the body is not usable, the sign-in works, or it does not. Check them in that order.
`req.body` is `undefined` when a request has no JSON body, so read it with a fallback. `typeof value === 'string'` tells text from everything else.

`const { email, password } = req.body ?? {}`, then a 400 when either is not a string that is not empty, then `const member = checkSignIn(staff, email, password)` and a 401 or `res.json({ staff: member })`.

tasks.title: Log each attempt without its secrets
tasks.description:
Make `POST /sign-in` log every attempt with `console.log`, so the studio can see who tried to sign in:

- one line per attempt with the email that was sent and how it ended
- no password and no password hash ever reaches the log, on any path and in any stream, or an answer

The check signs in right, wrong and with an unknown email, sends a body with no email and a body that is not JSON, and reads everything the app printed and every answer it sent.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js` and read what your route logs today.
List the secrets that pass through the route.
Write one line for a sign-in that worked and one for a refusal.
Run `node try.js` again and read every line.
hints: Two secrets pass through this route: the password that was typed, and the hash in the staff store. Neither may leave it.
Logging a whole object, `req.body` or a member from the store, copies everything inside it, the secret included. Build each line from the one fact you mean to log.
A line such as `` `signed in ${email}` `` after a good sign-in and `` `sign-in refused for ${email}` `` before the 401. Nothing else from the body.
